new.s: While a proclamation of National Emergency is in operation, the term of the Lok Sabha may be extended by law:
o: By one year at a time, but not beyond six months after the Emergency ceases to operate
By six months at a time, but not beyond one year after the Emergency ceases to operate
By one year at a time, without any limit after the Emergency ends
By two years in total, with the approval of the Supreme Court
new.x: Parliament may extend the term of the Lok Sabha (and of State Assemblies) by law for one year at a time during a National Emergency, but the extension cannot continue beyond six months after the Emergency ceases. The six-month unit, the absence of any limit and Supreme Court approval are all incorrect.
new.tq: 1 year at a time; 6 months after it ends.

new.s: President's Rule under Article 356 can be continued beyond one year only if:
o: A National Emergency is in operation or the Election Commission certifies that elections cannot be held
The Governor recommends it and the State Legislature consents
A National Emergency is in operation and the Election Commission certifies that elections cannot be held
Parliament approves it by a special majority every three months
new.x: Beyond one year, President's Rule needs both conditions together: a National Emergency in operation AND an Election Commission certificate that elections cannot be held. The 'or' version is the common trap. Governor's recommendation or state consent are not conditions, and approval is every six months (maximum three years), not every three months by special majority.
new.tq: Beyond 1 year: Emergency AND EC certificate - both.

Article 352 is National Emergency, Article 360 Financial Emergency, and Article 365 deems non-compliance with Union directions a breakdown but is not the President's Rule provision itself.

new.x: The Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) dealt with State funding of elections (partial funding in kind to recognised parties), not Centre-State relations. The Rajamannar Committee (1969), the Sarkaria Commission (1983) and the ARC (1966, Setalvad study team) all reviewed Centre-State relations.

new.s: A commission on Centre-State relations was constituted by the Union Government in June 1983 under a retired Supreme Court judge. It is:
new.x: The Sarkaria Commission was set up by the Centre in June 1983 under Justice R.S. Sarkaria, a retired Supreme Court judge, and reported in 1988 with 247 recommendations. The Rajamannar Committee (1969) was appointed by Tamil Nadu, the ARC dates to 1966, and the Punchhi Commission came later (2007).

new.x: The ARC recommended an Inter-State Council under Article 263, non-partisan Governors and more delegation and finances to States. Complete deletion of Article 356 was the Rajamannar Committee's demand, so any option with 3 is wrong, and '1 only' leaves out non-partisan Governors.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Inter-State Council:
1. It was set up in 1990 under Article 263 on the advice of the Sarkaria Commission.
2. It is chaired by the Union Home Minister.
3. Its 11th meeting was held on 16 July 2016.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
new.x: Statement 1 is correct: the ISC was set up in 1990 under Article 263 on Sarkaria's advice. Statement 3 is correct: its 11th meeting was held on 16 July 2016. Statement 2 is wrong: the Prime Minister chairs the Council; the Home Minister chairs its Standing Committee. So options with 2 are wrong.
new.tq: ISC: 1990, Sarkaria, PM chairs; last meeting 2016.
